title: Magnon Theory of Domain Wall Wavefronts and the Ballistic Diffusive Crossover in the Classical Anisotropic Landau Lifshitz Spin Chain
abstract: We study the far-from-equilibrium dynamics of domain-wall initial states in the integrable lattice Landau--Lifshitz spin chain. Building on the linear spin-wave description of domain-wall spreading, we derive the long-wavelength magnon dispersion directly from the microscopic integrable Hamiltonian and use it to characterize the propagation and broadening of the resulting wavefronts. The dispersion interpolates between a quadratic form at the isotropic point and a linear form in the easy-plane regime. In the isotropic limit, the quadratic dispersion leads to diffusive broadening, whereas in the easy-plane regime the domain-wall front propagates ballistically. Keeping the leading nonlinear correction to the linear dispersion gives a cubic dispersive term, which produces a characteristic $t^{1/3}$ broadening of the ballistic front. We further show that the sign of this cubic correction changes at a critical anisotropy, leading to a reversal of the dispersive wake from trailing to advancing. The resulting critical point occurs at $Δ_c=1/7$, corresponding to $γ_c\simeq 1.047$. Numerical simulations of the full nonlinear spin dynamics confirm the analytical scaling and demonstrate the coexistence of the amplitude-independent spin-wave front with amplitude-dependent nonlinear soliton propagation.
summary: This paper analyzes the non-equilibrium dynamics of domain walls in the anisotropic Landau-Lifshitz spin chain. It derives the magnon dispersion relation, showing how the system transitions between diffusive spreading (isotropic) and ballistic propagation (easy-plane). The key finding is the emergence of a characteristic $t^{1/3}$ subdiffusive broadening, which is governed by the cubic correction to the linear dispersion.
main_problem: The study characterizes the far-from-equilibrium dynamics of domain-wall initial states in the integrable lattice Landau-Lifshitz spin chain, focusing on the crossover between ballistic and diffusive wavefront propagation.
main_result: The wavefront dynamics exhibit a crossover from diffusive ($t^{1/2}$) scaling in the isotropic limit to ballistic propagation ($x \sim ct$) in the easy-plane regime, with subdiffusive broadening characterized by a $t^{1/3}$ exponent.
method: The analysis employs linear spin-wave theory derived from the microscopic Hamiltonian, supplemented by long-wavelength expansions and comparison with full nonlinear numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The system is the classical anisotropic Landau-Lifshitz spin chain, governed by a nearest-neighbor interaction Hamiltonian and the Landau-Lifshitz equation of motion.
key_observables: Wavefront spreading width ($\delta x$), magnon dispersion relation ($\omega(q)$), and the velocity of the propagating front.
important_parameters: Anisotropy parameter ($\Delta$), which dictates the crossover between regimes; the critical anisotropy point $\Delta_c = 1/7$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the linear spin-wave expansion for the initial characterization, though the results are confirmed by simulations of the full nonlinear dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnon dispersion relation across different anisotropies and compare the scaling of the spreading width in the diffusive ($t^{1/2}$) and subdiffusive ($t^{1/3}$) regimes.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the magnon dispersion relation from the microscopic Hamiltonian, analyzing its behavior in the isotropic and easy-plane limits, deriving the scaling laws for wavefront broadening, and finally confirming these analytical results using numerical simulations of the full nonlinear dynamics.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed, microscopic understanding of non-equilibrium transport phenomena (ballistic vs. diffusive) in a quantum-like spin system, which has parallels in understanding energy/information propagation in complex quantum many-body systems.

The long-wavelength behavior changes from quadratic at the isotropic point to linear in the easy-plane regime. The corre- sponding group velocity determines the ballistic propagation of the domain-wall wavefront.

The different regimes of the dispersive wavefront are illustrated through the corre- sponding scaling behavior.
